entry.title: Prizes for IceCube and MicroBooNE
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Francis Halzen was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. Separately, Fermilab's Sam Zeller received the W.K.H. Panofsky Prize for co-leadership of MicroBooNE, which advanced liquid-argon time projection chamber technology for neutrino detection.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab, CERN and SURF crews have started building the first of two cryostats, the large insulated containers that will hold liquid argon for DUNE. Fermilab news items from the following days describe the start of construction of the underground detector in South Dakota, and the roles of Colorado State University and the University of Texas at Arlington in detector development and construction.

entry.title: SBND electron-neutrino cross sections
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SBND at Fermilab measured the total and single-differential inclusive electron-neutrino charged-current cross sections on argon. The authors describe it as the highest-statistics inclusive measurement of this kind on argon to date, and the first using the Booster Neutrino Beam. Such measurements matter for electron-neutrino appearance searches in both long- and short-baseline oscillation programmes.

entry.title: JUNO ultrapure water
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. JUNO requires ultrapure water with a radium concentration below 50 μBq/m3 because the water is in direct contact with the liquid scintillator during filling. A paper describes a high-sensitivity radium measurement system and an optimised 100 t/h production process that combines selective ion-exchange resin with membrane separation.

entry.title: Geoneutrino decay test
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new analysis uses geoneutrinos to test neutrino decay for the first time, computing the visible-decay signal at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+ and JUNO and comparing it with their published data. It finds no evidence of decay that holds across Earth models, and combines the four experiments to set a limit on the ν1 to ν3 decay.

entry.title: ProtoDUNE muon seasonality
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The DUNE Collaboration measured seasonal variation of the cosmic-ray muon rate in the ProtoDUNE single-phase detector, using data from December 2018 to July 2020. The modulation has a significance of 4σ against no variation, with a maximum in winter, consistent with other surface experiments with a low muon-energy threshold.

entry.title: SHiP sterile-neutrino sensitivity
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The SHiP Collaboration shows that its baseline detector forms a two-baseline experiment for sterile-neutrino-induced oscillations. Neutrino interactions are recorded in the scattering and neutrino detector and, about 70 m further downstream, in the calorimeter system. The study uses a Geant4 simulation of Genie-generated interactions.

entry.title: Movable reactor at JUNO
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A phenomenology study considers a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within about 3 km of the JUNO detector. The aim is a precision on theta13 beyond that of Daya Bay, which the authors say no planned experiment is expected to surpass.

entry.title: IceCube neutral-current cross section
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A study investigates the sensitivity of IceCube to the neutral-current neutrino-nucleon cross section using 12 years of data. It considers two strategies: Earth absorption and regeneration, and the track-to-cascade event ratio. The authors note that neutral-current interactions remain largely unexplored experimentally at high energies.

entry.title: MINERvA open-data surrogate
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A probabilistic surrogate of the MINERvA detector response, trained on an open simulation dataset, maps generator-level final-state particles to reconstructed observables. It is meant to let people outside the collaboration test interaction models against open neutrino data without computationally intensive methods.

entry.title: The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars containing Δ isobars
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars containing Δ isobars. It matters because Urca processes are the dominant neutrino cooling mechanisms in neutron-star thermal evolution, and the Δ contribution had not been explicitly evaluated.

entry.title: The authors examine whether next-generation kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande can determine the
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors examine whether next-generation kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande can determine the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. They report that such detectors can differentiate between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even allowing for cross-section and hadronic-interaction uncertainties.

entry.title: The paper analyses neutrino production near the supermassive black hole in NGC 1068, using hadronic channels a
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper analyses neutrino production near the supermassive black hole in NGC 1068, using hadronic channels and cascade gamma rays together with Latin hypercube sampling of the parameter space. It is constrained by multimessenger data, including the updated IceCube data down to about 0.2 TeV.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: open two-flavour neutrino oscillations with evolution covariant under rotati
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: open two-flavour neutrino oscillations with evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane are exactly blind to a Majorana phase. A rate anisotropy in the decoherence can supply an environmental phase reference, which is the route by which a phase could become observable.

entry.title: The authors derive semianalytic approximations for the outcomes of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasiho
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors derive semianalytic approximations for the outcomes of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomogeneous neutrino ensembles. They report good agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of mass ordering, which offers a subgrid scheme for supernova simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics.

entry.title: The paper uses solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free da
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper uses solar neutrino-electron scattering data from PandaX-4T and XENONnT to constrain anomaly-free dark photon models with kinetic and mass mixing. It derives exclusion limits for six benchmark models and model-independent limits for pure kinetic and pure mass mixing.
